rv.q: Still, it’s difficult to see the audience participation in Becoming Hamlet as much more than a gimmick.

An interesting experiment, this version of Hamlet must be considered a failure as it adds nothing to the understanding of the play and those not very familiar with the original text will not be able to follow it.
This ripping apart of Shakespeare's arguably most famous creation was a grounding adventure for me.
I simply found its central device more gimmick than revelation.
Somewhere inside the production, there is an interesting perspective buried in its attempt to externalize Hamlet’s psychological conflict, but it never develops into a cohesive theatrical experience.
But the let's-all-play-Hamlet conceit proves to be more performative than profound.
Horowitz creates more than an inventive staging of Hamlet: he offers a rare chance to understand why Hamlet matters by making us part of the question.
The pacing is inconsistent, since it is dependent on the skills of several dozen nonprofessional actors.

cn.t: An ambitious participatory experiment invites audiences to inhabit Hamlet, earning praise for its visceral storytelling but dividing critics over whether the interactive concept truly unlocks Shakespeare or collapses under its own weight.
